title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 65-67): Grothendieck asks to what extent his section conjecture ('conjecture A or B') lets one reconstruct the category of elementary anabelian varieties over Q, and over finitely generated extensions of Q, purely from the data Γ_Q acting outerly on π̂_{0,3}. That action gives the extension E_{0,3} = E_{U_{0,3}/Q}, with U_{0,3} = P^1 − {0,1,∞}. On p.65 he takes the 'admissible' sections of E_{0,3} → Γ_Q, up to π̂-conjugacy. These are the points of the topos B^♮_{π̂_{0,3},Γ} over B^♮_Γ, and Γ acts on this set. He then picks a finite Γ-stable set I of such sections. Under the section conjecture these correspond to a Γ-stable finite set of points in U_{0,3}(Q̄).

This page: a group-theoretic 'forage des trous' (hole-drilling) at the sections in I should produce an outer group Π_{0,3}(I) of type (0, 3 + card I), still carrying an outer Γ-action. In modern terms this is the geometric π_1 of P^1 minus {0,1,∞} and the points of I, built from π̂_{0,3} with its Γ-action and the sections alone. To do this he suggests Raynaud's rigid-analytic yoga: take rigid discs (tubular neighbourhoods with boundary) centred at the holes 0, 1, ∞ and at the new points. Local inertia and decomposition groups then come from these discs.

He then proposes working with the 'groupoidal equivalent' of P^1_Q, which he names the 'sphère arithmétique'. He identifies it with E_{K_1}, K_1 = Q(T_1): the absolute Galois group of the purely transcendental extension of degree 1, as an extension of Γ_Q by Gal(Q̄(T)). It is the projective limit of the π_1 of all P^1 minus finitely many points, i.e. the birational, all-holes-drilled sphere. Starting from (6) one constructs the groupoidal U_{0,3} and climbs up step by step (p.67). One uses fibrations whose fibres are genus-0 curves of type (0,ν), or finite étale covers of such, over K_1, its finite extensions, or curves over Q. By successive elementary fibrations (Artin neighbourhoods) one reaches E_K for every finitely generated K/Q, and the elementary anabelian models. This also yields a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of every point of a smooth X/K.
errors: E_{K_1} = Gal(Q(T)^sep/Q) is not literally the groupoidal P^1. Geometric P^1 is simply connected; E_{K_1} is the generic-point / birational object, the limit over P^1 minus finite sets. Grothendieck's identification makes sense only in that birational sense.

Hole-drilling at an arbitrary admissible section is only meaningful if the section is geometric, i.e. comes from a point of U_{0,3}(Q̄) not equal to 0,1,∞. Tangential/cuspidal sections at 0,1,∞, or hypothetical non-geometric sections, would not give type (0,3+card I). The construction therefore presupposes the section conjecture plus a way of recognising the cuspidal sections, which is not addressed.

The rigid-geometry suggestion is only a sketch. How the local disc data would be recovered from the profinite group data alone, rather than from the variety, is left open; this is precisely the hard part of the cuspidalization problem.

ideas.what: Purely group-theoretic 'drilling of holes': from Γ_Q acting on π̂_{0,3}, plus a Γ-stable finite set of sections, construct the outer Galois action on π̂_1 of P^1 minus 3+|I| points.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mochizuki (Absolute anabelian cuspidalizations of proper hyperbolic curves, 2007); Hoshi, Minamide and others (2000s-2010s)
ideas.where_published: Not in the Esquisse or the letter to Faltings as such; only in these Longue Marche notes as far as I know

ideas.what: Use Raynaud's rigid geometry: discs around the punctures to obtain local (inertia/decomposition) data for drilled holes.
ideas.modern_name: Rigid/Berkovich tubular neighbourhoods; tangential base points; tempered fundamental group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); Ihara-Nakamura; André (tempered π_1); Mochizuki (p-adic anabelian)

ideas.what: 'Sphère arithmétique': the Galois group of Q(T) over Γ_Q, viewed as the groupoidal P^1_Q, i.e. the limit over all punctured lines.
ideas.modern_name: Birational anabelian geometry; absolute Galois group of a function field as the pro-limit of π_1 of open curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (birational anabelian conjecture, letter to Faltings 1983); proved by Pop (1994); birational section conjecture: Koenigsmann, Pop
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983) and Esquisse d'un programme (birational anabelian conjecture), though the name 'sphère arithmétique' appears unpublished

ideas.what: Climb from Q(T) and U_{0,3} by elementary fibrations of genus-0 curves (or their finite étale covers) to reconstruct E_K for all finitely generated K and all elementary anabelian varieties.
ideas.modern_name: Artin elementary neighbourhoods / good neighbourhoods; anabelian reconstruction via fibrations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Artin (SGA 4 XI); Grothendieck (Esquisse); Pop, Nakamura, Mochizuki for anabelian versions
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme / letter to Faltings mention elementary anabelian varieties

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly formulates the cuspidalization problem (genus 0, over Q) about two decades before Mochizuki made it central. He proposes rigid-analytic discs as the tool, and proposes a bootstrap: rebuild the whole anabelian category over finitely generated fields from Γ_Q acting on π̂_{0,3} plus the section conjecture.
missed.quote: "forage des trous" doit nous fournir du type (0,3+card I), un groupe extérieur Π_{0,3}(I), sur lequel Γ opère (il vaut mieux peut-être utiliser le yoga introduit par Raynaud des géométries rigides
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's priority for the cuspidalization idea. It also suggests a program, not fully realised, of reconstructing all of anabelian geometry over Q from U_{0,3} alone via section conjecture plus cuspidalization.

missed.claim: He links rigid-analytic local discs around punctures to group-theoretic hole-drilling, anticipating the use of p-adic/tempered or analytic neighbourhoods in reconstructing inertia data.
missed.quote: on fait un disque aux bords centrés en trous 0,1,∞
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a moderate historical connection; the modern theory (André, Mochizuki) developed it independently.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains an early, explicit formulation of the cuspidalization (hole-drilling) problem and the 'arithmetic sphere' = Gal(Q(T)) viewpoint. These ideas are now known under other names (Mochizuki, Pop), and the birational part is already in the letter to Faltings. It is historically interesting but not mathematically new.
transcription_corrections: 'chacun[?] on fait[?] un disque[?] aux[?] bords[?] centrés[?] en trous 0,1,∞' — sense is roughly 'i.e. on fait des disques à bords centrés aux trous 0,1,∞'; individual words remain uncertain.
Insertion '{+type,+}' near 'transcendante pure' probably belongs to 'l'extension transcendante pure type' (the standard purely transcendental extension).
'groupoïde à lacets {+est,+} défini' — reading uncertain; the inserted 'est' may modify 'qui correspond à ... est défini'.
